findings: No blocking correctness/privacy/authority bug found in the three in-scope files; verdict is APPROVE with non-blocking observations below.

Verified fail-closed boundaries: CPU-only and Drive-mount gates raise before any work; incomplete Drive scans block fresh copies; exclusive creates ('xb' opens, mkdir without parents, fresh UUID job dirs) prevent overwrites and start retries against the same job; destination checksum failure preserves both original and partial copy; receipts expose only exception class names while tracebacks stay in the private console log.

Verified privacy of persistent artifacts: receipt/status/packet/protocol files carry only pinned expectations, hashes, sizes, fixed paths, aggregate file counts, whitelisted status enum values, and bare PIDs; no archive bytes, in-archive filenames, command lines, or patient values are emitted; orchestrator artifacts are chmod 0600 and the Colab script runs under umask 0077.

Verified approval preservation: reviewed() requires an APPROVE artifact with matching scope and commit, response-file SHA-256 binding, a claude-fable-5 reviewer, and current-source staleness hashes over exactly the three in-scope files; the poll cell additionally asserts the on-Drive verify.py hash equals the currently reviewed source, so stale or tampered jobs fail closed.

Observation (identity binding): acquisition identity.json is hashed and its size/md5 agreement with the pinned constants is recorded as expected_binding_matches, but a mismatch or missing file never blocks preservation; enforcement rests solely on the source-pinned SIZE/MD5. Consider blocking or at least surfacing a distinct status on binding mismatch.

Observation (recovery/durability): an existing matching train.7z found under Shareddrives satisfies persistence without creating an operator-owned copy, though shared-drive members could later delete it; and the fresh-copy MD5 read-back goes through the same FUSE mount, so FRESH_DRIVE_COPY_VERIFIED is not an independent provider-side durability guarantee (the capacity check carries an analogous caveat; the persistence status does not).

Observation (concurrent starts): after a 600s orchestrator timeout the background job may still be running while status.json records FAILED; a subsequent start creates a second concurrent job whose capacity check races the first, risking a duplicate 92 GB copy or an ENOSPC partial. Each job still fails closed individually, and the job path recorded in packet.json/status.json enables polling the original instead.

Observation (post-hoc cell verification): verify_cell_sources runs after execution, so a same-user process that plants prompt-injection text in receipt.json has a narrow window to steer the dontAsk worker before validation fails; mitigated by the restricted mcp__colab-worker__* tool set, regex-constrained fresh 0700 job dirs, and JSON-only parsing of outputs. Worker actual_models is recorded but not enforced.

Scope limitation: imported helpers from orchestrator.colab_patient and orchestrator.colab_worker (CPU_CELL, verify_cell_sources, tool_exchanges, streams, write_private, private_dir) were not supplied and are assumed correct; the staleness gate pins only the three listed files, so those dependencies need their own review pinning.
